commits.message: test(rig): a rig records a render origin only when its session has none, so a seeded origin is never overwritten (candybar-testing-ihvy.4k6)
test(rig): the parse cache keys on each registered domain's members, rigs that seed an origin draw as that session, and the testing memory line is true again (candybar-testing-ihvy.4k6)
test(rig): the parse cache keys on the registered option domains (candybar-testing-ihvy.4k6)
test(rig): review fixes — undo-redo keeps its seeded origin, rig records its cwd, configure-mode keeps width 200 (candybar-testing-ihvy.4k6)

test(rig): 26 more test files build through buildRig, and buildRuntime is gone (candybar-testing-ihvy.4k6)

Each file keeps its own vocabulary as a thin wrapper over buildRig and no longer repeats the parse, store, registry, compile, draw and click assembly.

test(rig): buildRig assembles a render rig with a default for every field (candybar-testing-ihvy.4k6)

Foundation: test/helpers/rig.ts, its test, colour-256's measurement helpers in their own module, and dsl-groups, dsl-picker and colour-256 on the rig.

fix(test): the client's answer cases run over a memory connection on a held clock (candybar-testing-ihvy.5q4)

Three stub-daemon cases took the statusline's 50 ms connect and 150 ms total
budgets against a net server on the worker's own loop, so a loaded runner read
CONNECT_TIMEOUT or busy in place of the stub's reply (error-glyph: 1 of 40
loaded runs). What they prove is a decision, not an effect.

requestOutcome splits at the connect: exchangeOutcome is the round trip over a
stream already made, and requestOutcome is the connect plus that call. The
wire-code cases call renderOutcomeOf; the raw-bytes and glyph cases run
exchangeOutcome over memoryConnection() with a held clock. No socket, no wall
clock, no budget left to miss.

fix(git): a closed git cache answers a late declaration as closed, so no period re-arms after close (candybar-testing-ihvy.dbg)

A render mid-wait at close declared after close had dropped every repo,
built a fresh state on the closed cache, and that state's period re-armed
after every pass: hundreds of timers armed after daemon.close() returned.
fix(bar-pane): a frame overwrites its rows and lands whole, so the pane stops flickering (#558)

docs(design): the isolated daemon, tmux events and browser surface designs

Goals, architecture, contracts and one document per area, with the surveys and probes behind them. The Frame is recorded as built, and the browser surface is un-parked.
